paragraphs.title: Song, Salvation, and the Proclamation of God's Wonders

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “Sing unto the LORD, all the earth.”
easy.q: Who is called to sing a new song unto the LORD?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 commands God's people to show forth “his salvation from day to day.”
easy.q: What are people commanded to show forth from day to day?

easy.explanation: Verse 3 says, “Declare his glory among the heathen.”
easy.q: Among whom should God's glory be declared?

medium.explanation: The verses move from singing and blessing God's name to proclaiming salvation and declaring His glory.
Verse 2 specifically says to show forth “his salvation from day to day.”
medium.q: What is to be proclaimed from day to day?

medium.explanation: God's wonders are His extraordinary and marvelous deeds.
medium.q: What does the word “wonders” refer to in verse 3?

answers: Worship is a central response to God
challenge.explanation: The repeated command highlights singing and worship as important responses to God.
challenge.q: What does the repeated command to sing unto the LORD emphasize?

answers: They all call for proclaiming God's greatness
They all describe the creation of heaven
They all discuss judgment of the nations
challenge.explanation: Singing, blessing, showing forth salvation, and declaring God's wonders all proclaim His greatness.

answers: The message of salvation should continue regularly
The message should be given only once a year
The message belongs only to the past
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates an ongoing, daily proclamation of God's salvation.
challenge.q: What does “from day to day” imply in this passage?

answers: Great and greatly to be praised
easy.explanation: Verse 4 says, “For the LORD is great, and greatly to be praised.”
easy.q: How is the LORD described in verse 4?

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “For all the gods of the nations are idols.”
easy.q: How are the gods of the nations described?

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “but the LORD made the heavens.”

answers: The powerless idols versus the LORD who made the heavens
medium.explanation: The passage contrasts the idols of the nations with the LORD, the Maker of the heavens.
medium.q: What is the main contrast in verses 4–5?

medium.explanation: Verse 6 mentions honour, majesty, strength, and beauty.
medium.q: What qualities are associated with the LORD and His sanctuary?

medium.explanation: The idols are contrasted with the living LORD and are presented as powerless false objects of worship.
medium.q: What does “idols” mean in the context of verse 5?

answers: It presents Him as the powerful Creator
It describes the joy of the forest
It recalls the offerings of the nations
challenge.explanation: The LORD's creation of the heavens demonstrates His power and distinguishes Him from idols.
challenge.q: Why does mentioning that the LORD made the heavens strengthen the description of His supremacy?

answers: His honour and majesty are associated with His sanctuary
The sanctuary belongs to the idols
The sanctuary is described as empty
challenge.explanation: Verse 6 connects the LORD's splendour and strength with His sanctuary.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the movement from the LORD's glory to His sanctuary?

challenge.explanation: The phrase “greatly to be praised” intensifies the description of the LORD's praise.
challenge.q: Which word most strongly emphasizes the greatness of the praise given to the LORD?

paragraphs.title: The Nations Called to Worship God

easy.explanation: Verse 7 addresses “the kindreds of the people.”
easy.q: Who is called to give glory and strength unto the LORD?

easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, “bring an offering, and come into his courts.”
easy.q: What are people told to bring into the LORD's courts?

easy.explanation: Verse 10 says, “Say among the heathen that the LORD reigneth.”
easy.q: What are people to say among the heathen?

answers: Give glory, bring an offering, worship, and proclaim God's reign
medium.explanation: The verses describe a progression of honoring God, bringing an offering, worshiping Him, and declaring His kingship.
medium.q: What order of actions is presented in verses 7–10?

answers: The world is established and He judges righteously
The heavens disappear and the sea becomes still
medium.explanation: Verse 10 says the world shall be established and that the LORD shall judge the people righteously.
medium.q: What is said to happen after the proclamation that the LORD reigneth?

answers: A gift or sacrifice brought to God
medium.explanation: The offering is something presented to God in worship.
medium.q: What is an “offering” in the context of verse 8?

answers: Both express reverence before the LORD
Both describe the making of the sea
Both show the weakness of the nations
challenge.explanation: Worshiping the LORD and fearing before Him both express reverence and awe.
challenge.q: How are worship and fear connected in verse 9?

answers: The call to worship extends to many peoples
The call is limited to one family
The call is addressed only to the sanctuary
challenge.explanation: The phrase presents a broad invitation to the families and peoples of the nations.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “kindreds of the people” suggest?

answers: His reign is proclaimed alongside a world that will not be moved
His reign causes the earth to disappear
The verse makes no connection between them
challenge.explanation: The verse joins the declaration that the LORD reigneth with the world's being established and not moved.
challenge.q: How are the LORD's reign and the world's stability connected in verse 10?

easy.explanation: Verse 11 says, “Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad.”
Verse 11 says, “let the sea roar, and the fulness thereof.”
Verse 13 says that the LORD comes “to judge the earth.”

answers: The heavens, earth, sea, field, and trees of the wood
medium.explanation: The passage names the heavens, earth, sea, field, and trees as participants in the rejoicing.
medium.q: Which parts of creation are mentioned in verses 11–12?

medium.explanation: Verse 12 says, “Let the field be joyful,” and that the trees of the wood shall rejoice.
medium.q: What do the field and the trees of the wood do?

medium.explanation: In this context, “the world” refers to the whole inhabited earth.
medium.q: What does “the world” refer to in verse 13?

answers: Creation rejoices in anticipation of His righteous judgment
Creation is afraid and therefore becomes inactive
The joy has no connection with His coming
challenge.explanation: The passage presents creation's joy as occurring before the LORD comes to judge righteously.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between creation's joy and the LORD's coming to judge?

answers: From the heavens and earth to the sea, field, and trees
From the sanctuary to kings only
From the nations to idols only
challenge.explanation: The passage progressively includes more parts of creation in the rejoicing.
challenge.q: How does the picture of joy expand in verses 11–12?

challenge.explanation: Verse 13 says He will judge the world “with righteousness” and the people “with his truth.”
challenge.q: By what two standards does the LORD judge in verse 13?
